spec: Title or variant states N16R8 (16 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM). Module is ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 with the PCB antenna, not the -1U external-antenna part. Two USB-C ports preferred (native USB plus UART bridge). 44 pin DevKitC-1 footprint.
why: The main MCU of the gateway and of the mains relay: 16 MB flash holds the captive portal and the receipt log, 8 MB PSRAM holds the session table, and the two USB-C ports let the native USB port stay free while the bridge carries the console.

candidates.title: ESP32-S3 Development Board with Expansion Adapter Kit 2.4G Wifi BT Module MCU ESP32-S3WROOM1 N16R8 44Pin Type-C ESP32S3
candidates.price_note: KSh 572 is the figure shown on the listing for the plain board. The listing also sells dearer variants: external IPEX antenna, a GPIO extension board and a power supply board. Order the onboard-antenna, board-only variant. No Choice or Welcome badge seen.
candidates.notes: Verified in Chrome 2026-09-14: the 572 figure is the S3 Expansion Board B variant and no variant of this listing names N16R8. Only candidate where the module label was legible and genuine. Gallery image 2, the pin definition sheet, shows the shield printed ESP32-S3 with the CE mark, ID 2ACZ2-ESPS3WROOM1, IC 21098-ESPS3WROOM1 and N16R8 underneath. Those are Espressif's own FCC and IC identifiers for ESP32-S3-WROOM-1, so the module is the real part and not a relabelled clone. The same drawing shows the black PCB antenna at the top of the shield, 44 broken-out pins, and two USB-C connectors wired to GPIO19 and GPIO20 (native USB) and to the bridge. Landed cost for the pair is KSh 1,144 plus whatever shipping the cart adds; the scraper could not read the shipping line, so treat shipping as unconfirmed.

candidates.notes: Rejected on the photo check. The first gallery image is a sharp close-up and the module shield reads SparkleIoT, MODEL XH-S3E, N16R8, with a local SRRC mark and a U.FL connector fitted next to the PCB antenna. That is a third party module in the WROOM-1 footprint, not an Espressif ESP32-S3-WROOM-1, so the firmware pin map may hold but the RF part and the flash vendor are unknown. Second reason: image 2 prints N8R2 / N16R8 as the choice, so the headline price is not certainly the 16 MB part.
